item.title: inventory-client: listItems follows next_cursor
item.brief:
Operator request (authenticated, local socket): inventory-api's `GET /items` is becoming cursor-paginated. Update inventory-client to use it.

API contract the client must follow:
- `GET /items` accepts optional `limit` (1..100, default 20) and `cursor` (opaque string from a previous response).
- Response body is `{"items": [...], "next_cursor": <string or null>}`. Items are ordered by `id`. `next_cursor` is null on the last page.
- Invalid parameters return HTTP 400 with `{"error": "..."}`.

Client requirements:
- `listItems(transport)` must still resolve to every item, in order, by following `next_cursor` until it is null (or absent), passing the cursor back unchanged. The first request sends no cursor.
- Keep functions under 60 lines; fail visibly on unexpected responses (do not swallow errors).
- Update the repository README to document the behaviour.
- Keep tests passing (`npm test`) and add tests for multi-page results, a single page, and a missing `next_cursor` field.
- Commit on the local branch. Do not push. Use the repository's existing git identity; do not override it.

pr.body: Approach: listItems loops over GET /items. The first request sends no cursor; each later request passes the previous next_cursor back unchanged as the cursor query param. Missing or null next_cursor ends the loop. Guards: non-200 responses reject via request(); a body without an items array, a non-string next_cursor, or a repeated cursor throws. Key files: client.js (listItems, pageItems, nextCursor), test/client.test.js (multi-page, single page, missing next_cursor, later-page error, repeated cursor, malformed page, non-string cursor), README.md. Checks: npm test 10/10 passing on 9647ce9. Assumptions: the server default page size (20) is used; no limit is sent. Open follow-ups (non-blocking): an empty-string next_cursor is treated as a cursor, not as end-of-listing.
pr.summary: listItems now returns every item across all GET /items pages. before: one page only; now: follows next_cursor until null or absent, malformed or failed pages reject.

item.title: inventory-api: cursor pagination for GET /items
item.brief:
Operator request (authenticated, local socket): `GET /items` in inventory-api returns every item in one response, which no longer scales. Add cursor pagination.

Contract (must be implemented exactly):
- `GET /items` accepts optional query parameters `limit` (integer 1..100, default 20) and `cursor` (an opaque string taken from a previous response).
- Response body becomes `{"items": [...], "next_cursor": <string or null>}`. Items stay ordered by `id`. `next_cursor` is null on the last page.
- An invalid `limit` (non-integer or outside 1..100) or an invalid `cursor` gets HTTP status 400 with body `{"error": "..."}`.

Requirements:
- Validate inputs at the boundary; keep functions under 60 lines and add meaningful assertions/validation where risky.
- Update the repository README to document the new parameters and response shape.
- Keep the existing test suite passing (`python3 -m unittest`) and add tests for: default page size, paging through all items with cursors, last page having next_cursor null, invalid limit and invalid cursor returning 400.
- Commit on the local branch. Do not push. Use the repository's existing git identity; do not override it.

Commits: 84fb355 (feature, api.py, test_api.py, README.md) and 0b5f835 (fixes from review). Default page size is 20 (limit 1..100); cursor is an opaque base64 of the last returned id; next_cursor is null on the last page; invalid limit or cursor returns 400 {"error": ...}. Before: one response with all 57 items and no next_cursor. Now: first page of 20 plus next_cursor. Checks: python3 -m unittest, 11 tests OK on the final head, including the required default size, full paging, last-page null, and 400 cases. pr.body: Approach: parse_limit and parse_cursor validate query values at the boundary and raise BadRequest, which handle() converts to HTTP 400. The cursor is base64 of the last returned id; list_items returns items with id greater than that id, sorted by id, up to limit, and sets next_cursor when more candidates remain. Digit strings are capped at 18 characters so int() never sees oversized input. Key files: api.py, test_api.py, README.md. Checks: python3 -m unittest, 11 tests OK on 0b5f835. Assumptions: the cursor format is internal and opaque; clients that expect every item from GET /items must now follow next_cursor. Follow-ups: get_item still uses isdigit()/int() (pre-existing, outside this diff); cursor parsing accepts standard base64 '+' and '/'.
pr.summary: Made GET /items paginate: limit (1..100, default 20) and opaque cursor query params. Now: each response is one page with next_cursor (null on last page). Before: every item in one response with no next_cursor. Invalid limit or cursor returns 400.
pr.title: Add cursor pagination to GET /items

risk.why: Changes the public GET /items contract: default page size 20 truncates responses for existing callers, new next_cursor key, new 400 paths. Touches api.py, test_api.py and README.md; behaviour changes, not only tests and docs. Eleven unit tests pass. Three whole-change reviews found blocking validation bugs, all fixed; a delta review passed.
